$comment: Canonical MCP tool descriptors for mcp.smarterweather.com. Generated by services/sw-mcp/scripts/dump-tool-descriptors.ts in the private repo -- do not edit by hand.

tools.name: compare_locations
tools.title: Compare locations
tools.description: Compare forecast variables across multiple locations side-by-side in one batched call. Returns a distilled per-location series matrix for direct comparison -- prefer this over N sequential forecast calls. Locations accept place names directly. Example: {"locations": [{"location": "Denver, CO"}, {"location": "Boulder, CO"}], "variables": ["temperature_2m", "precipitation_probability"], "hours": 48}.

location.description: "City, ST", ZIP, or "lat,lon" (e.g. "Boulder, CO").

locations.description: Locations to compare (2-10). Each takes location OR lat/lon, optional label.

dataset_id.description: Dataset override. Default: auto-resolved NBM per location.

units.description: Variables without a unit label stay native.

errors.description: Locations left out of comparisons, by input index: outside coverage.

attribution.description: Attribution the dataset licence requires. Cite it when quoting these values.

tools.name: describe_dataset
tools.title: Describe dataset
tools.description: A dataset's variables (standard names, units, display units, categories, bands), horizon, step, cadence, freshness, cost class and an example_query for query_dataset. Example: {"dataset_id": "nbm_conus"}.

dataset_id.description: Pipeline dataset identifier (e.g. "nbm_conus", "mrms_reflectivity_conus"). Discover valid values with list_datasets; inspect variables with describe_dataset.

example_query.description: query_dataset arguments for this dataset; add a location.

data_status.description: Present only when the data service could not answer: a cached copy, or catalog facts without freshness.

attribution.description: Attribution the dataset licence requires. Cite it when quoting these values.

tools.name: find_best_window
tools.title: Find best weather window
tools.description: Find the optimal time window for an activity based on weather criteria. Scans the forecast and returns daylight-aware periods matching all conditions. Criteria are expressed in the selected `units` system (default imperial: °F, mph, miles, feet). Example: {"location": "Boulder, CO", "criteria": {"min_temperature": 55, "max_wind_speed": 15, "max_precipitation_probability": 20}, "hours": 72, "activity_duration_hours": 3}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

min_temperature.description: Minimum temperature in the selected units (°F / °C / K).

max_temperature.description: Maximum temperature in the selected units (°F / °C / K).

max_wind_speed.description: Maximum sustained wind in the selected units (mph / km/h / m/s).

max_wind_gust.description: Maximum wind gust in the selected units (mph / km/h / m/s).

min_visibility.description: Minimum visibility in the selected units (miles / km / m).

min_ceiling.description: Minimum cloud ceiling in the selected units (feet / m / m).

criteria.description: Weather criteria defining acceptable conditions (all optional).

activity_duration_hours.description: Minimum consecutive hours meeting criteria. Default 2.

daylight_only.description: Only consider daylight hours (sunrise to sunset). Default true.

activity.description: Free-form activity to rate the windows for (e.g. "afternoon golf"). Accepted even when rating is off so clients can send it.

tools.name: get_air_quality
tools.title: Get air quality
tools.description: AirNow air quality at a location (CONUS): current overall AQI plus per-pollutant AQI sub-indices (PM2.5, ozone, PM10) and the AirNow AQI forecast. AQI scale: 0-50 good, 51-100 moderate, 101-150 unhealthy for sensitive groups, 151-200 unhealthy, 201-300 very unhealthy, 301+ hazardous. pollutants=["aqi"] (default) is the cheap headline call; add pollutant keys or include_forecast=true when the user digs in. Example: {"location": "Boise, ID", "pollutants": ["aqi", "pm25"], "include_forecast": true}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

pollutants.description: Which measurements to return. aqi = combined AQI index. Default: ["aqi"].

include_forecast.description: Also return the AirNow next-day AQI forecast.

units.description: Every value is an AQI or AQI sub-index, not a concentration.
Every value is an AQI or AQI sub-index, not a concentration.

widget.description: sw-ui-spec widget block rendered by the MCP Apps weather widget (ui://weather-widget/v1/index.html). Additive; safe to ignore.

tools.name: get_alerts
tools.title: Get NWS alerts
tools.description: NWS watches, warnings, advisories. Point (city/ZIP/lat+lon): containing polygons. BBox or US state/DC/CONUS (codes, full names, US/national): intersecting polygons. A city miss is not a statewide all-clear — query the state or a bbox; never say regional inventory is impossible. NY/WA and "New York State"/"Washington State" are states; "New York"/"Washington" stay cities. Omit at for now; at (ISO-8601 UTC) is the snapshot then. Empty = all-clear or purged (~24h). alert_id = detail+geometry, ignores at. Ex: {"location":"WI","events":["Tornado Warning"]}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

bbox.description: Bounding box {west,south,east,north}; west/east are negative in the US. Skips geocoding; intersecting polygons.

alert_id.description: Alert identifier for detail mode. When set, location is ignored.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC past instant for the in-effect snapshot. Ignored with alert_id.

valid_time.description: Echo of at when an as-of snapshot was requested.

widget.description: sw-ui-spec widget block rendered by the MCP Apps weather widget (ui://weather-widget/v1/index.html). Additive; safe to ignore.

tools.name: get_climate_normals
tools.title: Get climate normals
tools.description: Day-of-year climate normals (NCEI 1991-2020 30-year averages) for a US location, from the nearest station with a record: normal high, low and mean per date, plus the station and its distance. Use this whenever a question needs a baseline rather than a forecast: "is this warm for October?", "what is a typical high here in January?", "how does this week compare to normal?". Pair it with get_forecast to say how far above or below normal the coming days run. Answers for any date, past or future: long-period averages, not a forecast or one year's observations.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

start.description: Inclusive range start as YYYY-MM-DD. Must be supplied with end.

end.description: Inclusive range end as YYYY-MM-DD. Must be supplied with start.

days.description: Range length in days when start/end are omitted; the window opens today (default 14).

tools.name: get_climate_records
tools.title: Get climate reports and records
tools.description: NWS daily climate data: type=reports returns CLI daily climate reports (observed high/low/precip vs normals per station); type=records returns RER record event reports (record highs/lows/rainfall actually set). Filter by wfo (3-letter office, e.g. DMX), station, date (YYYY-MM-DD), start/end range, or hours lookback. Examples: {"type": "records", "hours": 48} or {"type": "reports", "wfo": "DMX", "date": "2026-07-04"}.

type.description: reports = CLI daily climate reports; records = RER record events.

record_type.description: Record type filter (records only), e.g. HIGH, LOW, RAIN.

hours.description: Lookback window in hours (1-168) when no date/range is given.

tools.name: get_current_conditions
tools.title: Get current conditions
tools.description: Current weather right now at a location from two independent sources in one call: the RTMA gridded analysis (exact-point values, updated sub-hourly) and the nearest METAR station observation (ground truth with raw METAR, flight category). Use the analysis for point-accurate values and the station for verification. Analysis fields: temperature_2m, dew_point_2m, relative_humidity_2m (derived here from temperature and dew point; listed in analysis.derived), wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m, wind_gusts_10m, surface_pressure (station pressure at ground level, not sea-level pressure), visibility, cloud_cover, cloud_ceiling, in units (labels in analysis.unit_labels). nearest_station is the station's own report, unconverted. For a forecast, use get_forecast. Example: {"location": "Pella, IA"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: imperial (default; °F, mph, inHg, mi, ft) or metric (°C, km/h, hPa, km, m); si returns K, m/s, Pa, m. si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric. Not applied to nearest_station.

tools.name: get_forecast
tools.title: Get forecast
tools.description: Complete weather overview for a location: current conditions, daily forecast (SPC threats, severity; view "detailed" adds CAPE, UV, full day/night periods), active alerts, and outlooks in one call. Pre-aggregated across NBM, HRRR, GFS, RTMA, and SPC and unit-converted server-side. Primary weather tool; reach for lower-level tools only when you need raw observations or a specific dataset. Times are UTC ISO 8601; quote daily[].astro.local to users, not UTC. If forecast.location.timezone_resolved is false, zone unknown: state times as UTC, never as local. Accepts a place name directly. Examples: {"location": "Denver, CO"} or {"location": "Portland, OR", "days": 5} or {"lat": 41.4, "lon": -92.9}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

include.description: Comma-separated sections: current, daily, hourly, alerts, outlooks. Default "current,daily,alerts,outlooks". Use get_hourly_forecast for hourly detail.

view.description: concise (default; REST's is detailed), ~5-10KB: daily has day_precip_probability / night_precip_probability (precip_probability is their max). detailed, ~12-20KB: adds CAPE, UV, full day/night periods, extra hourly fields.

data_status.description: Present only when the platform reports degraded/outage data sources: overall state, a caveat note, and the affected sources. Absent means no advisory was available -- not a freshness guarantee. See get_platform_status for the full document.

widget.description: sw-ui-spec widget block rendered by the MCP Apps weather widget (ui://weather-widget/v1/index.html). Additive; safe to ignore.

tools.name: get_forecast_discussion
tools.title: Get forecast discussion
tools.description: Expert forecaster text products. type=afd: Area Forecast Discussion. type=hwo: Hazardous Weather Outlook. type=now: WFO short-term NOW. type=fwf/hls/esf: local fire weather / hurricane local statement / hydrologic discussion. type=mcd: SPC Mesoscale Discussion. type=mpd: WPC Mesoscale Precipitation Discussion (flash flood). type=swo/fwd/ero: national outlook discussions. type=tcd/tcp/tcm/twd/two: NHC tropical text (type=two is the text TWO, not GIS nhc_two). type=pmd: WPC/CPC desk discussion (pass awips_id for a specific desk, e.g. PMDSPD). type=pwo: SPC public weather outlook. National types (swo/fwd/ero/tcd/tcp/tcm/twd/two/pmd/pwo) need no location; `day` selects the outlook day for swo and fwd. summary_only=true returns an AI-written summary, not the full body. Examples: {"location": "Des Moines, IA", "type": "afd"} or {"type": "swo", "day": 2, "summary_only": true}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

type.description: Product type: afd (WFO discussion), hwo (hazard outlook), now (short-term NOW), fwf/hls/esf (local WFO), mcd (SPC mesoscale), mpd (WPC precipitation discussion), swo (SPC convective outlook), fwd (SPC fire weather), ero (WPC excessive rainfall), tcd/tcp/tcm/twd/two (NHC tropical text; two is text TWO not GIS), pmd (desk discussion), pwo (SPC public outlook).

day.description: Outlook day for type=swo or type=fwd (1-8). Ignored for the other types; WPC files ERO days 1-3 under one product.

awips_id.description: AWIPS id (e.g. TCDAT1, PMDSPD; CPC: PMDMRD 6-10/8-14d, PMD34D wk3-4, PMD30D 30d, PMD90D 90d, PMDTHR hazards, PMDENS ENSO). Exact source_ref; beats type+location.

wfo.description: WFO identifier override (e.g. BOU). Default: resolved from the location.

summary_only.description: Return only the LLM summary + sections, omitting the full body text.

tools.name: get_forecast_distribution
tools.title: Get forecast distribution
tools.description: NBM probabilistic guidance for one weather aspect: percentiles (p10-p90), exceedance probabilities and ensemble spread. Use this for any question about odds, ranges, potential or confidence ("how much could we get", "range of possible highs", "how sure is this") -- a deterministic forecast value cannot answer one. Reading the percentiles: p50 is the most likely outcome, p90 is the reasonable worst case when the risk is the high end (snow totals, wind, rainfall), and p10 when the risk is the low end (cold, visibility, ceiling). A single percentile is not the forecast -- report the likely value with the tail that matters, and label which is which. Aspects: precip (PoP, QPF + percentiles), snow (accumulation percentiles, >1/2/4in probabilities, snow level, snow-type probability), ice (ice accretion, freezing-rain / ice-pellet probabilities), temperature (`daily` high/low p10/p50/p90: the NBM value -/+ 1.28 stddev; hourly temp + stddev), wind (speed/gust percentiles), severe (thunderstorm probability plus NBM CWASP, a severe-environment index, both in percent: severe_weather_prob_p50 is the median CWASP value and severe_weather_prob_above_75 the probability CWASP exceeds 75; NBM has no tornado, hail or damaging-wind odds; SPC's: get_outlooks (guidance) hazard=severe), aviation (LIFR/IFR/MVFR visibility + ceiling odds), confidence (ensemble stddev; low = settled, high = details still in play). Labels in unit_labels. Example: {"location": "Denver, CO", "aspect": "snow", "hours": 72}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric. si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

tools.name: get_forecast_skill
tools.title: Get forecast skill
tools.description: How accurate our forecasts have actually been near a location, measured against observed analysis truth. Returns bias (positive = the model runs high), mean absolute error, RMSE, and a skill score against local climatology, per model, weather variable, and forecast lead time; continuous and vector entries also carry persistenceSkillScore, skill against the analysis at forecast issue time (null means not enough persist pairs, not zero skill -- do not compare it to skillScore as if they shared a denominator), and analysisDisagreementMae, the analyses' own disagreement at that lead -- a floor on how good the forecast can look, not a skill score and not an excuse (null means the sibling row is missing or below minimumSamples); for probability forecasts, the Brier score and a reliability breakdown. Use this to qualify a forecast rather than assert it -- "NBM has been running 1.8F warm at 3-day leads near you, so treat that 72 as around 70" -- and to answer "how much should I trust this forecast", "is the model biased here", or "how accurate were you last month". Evidence comes at three scopes side by side: the exact point (strongest, slowest to accumulate), the neighborhood and the region (coarse pooled cells, not street-level). Prefer the most specific scope that has samples. Metrics below minimumSamples observations are withheld and listed under insufficientHistory with their count -- say history is still accumulating; do not treat thin numbers as evidence. Coverage is a rolling recent window over verified US variables, not all of history. Samples aren't matched across models, so never conclude one model beats another from these numbers. Each entry states the truth field it was measured against (one designated analysis per variable); never compare numbers with different truth values either. Each entry also states its regime: ALL (every observation, any weather) or a conditioned tier such as SEA:DJF (winter), SCN1:WINDY / SCN1:WET / SCN1:QUIET (what the forecast was showing), or JC1:NW (a circulation pattern). Pass the regime parameter to ask for a conditioned track record. It falls back: asking for SCN1:WINDY and getting regime ALL is a successful answer, not a missing one -- always read the regime field and qualify the claim with it, because "NBM runs warm here when it shows windy" and "NBM runs warm here" are different statements. Regimes overlap by construction across families, so entries under different regimes are alternative answers to one question; never compare or add them. Within SCN1: the labels are mutually exclusive. Entries with a categorical block answer a yes/no question instead of an error magnitude -- did it rain, at the thresholdMm stated on the entry -- with pod (of the times it happened, how often we called it), far (of the times we called it, how often it did not happen), and frequencyBias (above 1 = we call it too often). Use these for "will it actually rain" questions, where a small average error means nothing if the rain lands in the wrong hour. A null rate means the sample cannot answer it -- the event has not happened, or been forecast, enough times to divide by -- and must be reported as unknown, never as zero. The counts beside it are still evidence, and for a rare event they are often the whole answer: "it has only rained twice here in the record" is a useful thing to say.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

variable.description: Narrow to one variable, e.g. temperature_2m, dew_point_2m, wind_speed_10m, wind_gusts_10m, wind_vector_10m, cloud_cover, precipitation, precipitation_probability, or a thresholded rain event such as precipitation_gt_0p254mm (any measurable rain) or precipitation_gt_2p54mm. Omit for everything measured at the location.

model.description: Narrow to one model, e.g. nbm or rrfs.

lead_hours.description: Narrow to the lead time being asked about, in hours; the containing lead bucket is selected for you (60 gives the 48-72h bucket). Use the lead of the forecast you are qualifying: ~24 for tomorrow, ~72 for three days out. Never approximated -- a lead we have not verified returns no entries rather than a nearby bucket, so an empty result means we cannot speak to that range.

truth.description: Measure against a named truth source instead of the default one for each variable, e.g. urma. Only pass this if the user asked which analysis was used or named one; the default is already the designated source, and the analyses disagree, so switching changes the numbers.

regime.description: Ask for a track record measured only under particular conditions, as a comma-separated preference chain, most specific first, e.g. "SCN1:WINDY,SEA:JJA". SEA: is the meteorological season (DJF, MAM, JJA, SON); SCN1: is a forecast-conditioned scenario (WINDY, WET, QUIET — mutually exclusive within the family); JC1: is a circulation pattern. The most specific tier with enough observations answers and the unconditioned record is the last resort, so this never empties a result the way truth does -- it degrades. Read the regime field on each entry to see which tier actually answered. Pass this when the question is conditional ("is it worse in winter", "how does it do when the model shows windy"); omit it otherwise, since conditioned tiers are thinner and slower to earn numbers.

unit.description: Deprecated: use units. si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

tracked.description: Whether this exact coordinate is one the verification pipeline tracks.

tools.name: get_forecast_skill_map
tools.title: Get forecast skill map
tools.description: Measured forecast skill as a map of ~50 km hexes inside a bounding box, sliced from the public skill map. Use this when the question is spatial ("where is NBM temperature skill weak across Colorado"), not "how good is the forecast at this point" — that is get_forecast_skill. Requires model, variable, lead_hours, and bbox {west,south,east,north}. lead_hours selects the containing published bucket (20 → NBM 24); a lead we have not published returns no slices rather than a nearby one. A hex is included when its center is inside the box; edge-overlapping hexes are dropped. The box cannot wrap the dateline. Each cell is [h3, samples, skill_score]; skill_score is unitless (fraction of climatological variance explained) and already gated at n ≥ 30. withheld lists hexes still accumulating. Do not compare slices across models or truths. Cells are areas; never treat a hex as a person.

bbox.description: Bounding box {west,south,east,north}; west/east are negative in the US. Hexes whose H3 center falls inside are returned.

model.description: Model id, e.g. nbm, gfs, hrrr, or rrfs.

variable.description: Verified variable, e.g. temperature_2m, dew_point_2m, precipitation, or precipitation_gt_0p254mm.

lead_hours.description: Lead time in hours; the containing published bucket is selected. Never approximated.

domain.description: Optional domain (conus, alaska, hawaii). Omit unless you already know it.

tools.name: get_growing_degree_days
tools.title: Get growing degree days
tools.description: Growing Degree Units (GDU / GDD) for a US location, computed from daily max/min temperatures. crop picks calibrated base/upper thresholds; crop="custom" takes base_temp_c (and optional upper_temp_c / method). Without season_start you get per-day GDU across the forecast horizon; WITH season_start you get the cumulative season-to-date total (observed history + today + forecast) plus a per-day cumulative series -- the number a grower tracks against crop milestones. Answers "how many growing degree days has my corn accumulated since May 1?" and "what's the GDU forecast this week?".

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

crop.description: Crop id from the catalog (e.g. "corn", "soybean", "wheat"), or "custom" with base_temp_c.

season_start.description: Season/planting start, YYYY-MM-DD local, within the last ~180 days.

day_definition.description: Daily boundary: "nws" (default; NBM MaxT/MinT period extremes) or "local_calendar" (midnight-to-midnight local day).

base_temp_c.description: Custom base threshold in °C. Required when crop="custom".

upper_temp_c.description: Custom upper cutoff in °C (enables the modified method).

method.description: GDU method for custom crops. Defaults from whether upper_temp_c is set.

include_milestones.description: Add the crop's growth-stage GDU milestones.

tools.name: get_hourly_forecast
tools.title: Get hourly forecast
tools.description: Blended hourly forecast: temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, precipitation probability/amount, conditions, and icon per hour. hourly[0] is the current or next hour; hourly_coverage.first_time says which. Timestamps are UTC ISO 8601; convert to the local timezone before presenting. Ask for the days you need up front -- one call with days: 4 beats four calls. ALWAYS check hourly_coverage before answering about a specific hour: it reports first_time and last_time (the window the rows actually span), sample_interval_hours (past the first day rows are every 2-3h, not every hour), and truncated: true when upstream returned less than you asked for. If the hour the user cares about is after last_time, say the forecast does not reach that far yet rather than answering from the nearest row you do have. For one stretch of time ask for that stretch with hours_from/hours_to: it comes back hour by hour even where the full range would be sampled. Accepts a place name or coordinates. Examples: {"location": "Portland, OR", "days": 2} or {"lat": 41.88, "lon": -87.63, "hours_from": 36, "hours_to": 48}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

days.description: Days of hourly data (1-7). Default 2. Widened when hours_to reaches further.

hours_from.description: Window start, in hours from now (0 = the current hour).

hours_to.description: Window end, in hours from now, exclusive. 36 to 48 is hours 36-47.

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

view.description: concise (default) samples past 24h; detailed adds CAPE, ceiling, UV, gust and thunderstorm probability for 48h.

tools.name: get_lightning_activity
tools.title: Get lightning activity
tools.description: Real-time lightning near a location: GLM satellite flash count and MRMS ground-truth lightning density + 30-minute probability. The summary field is ready-to-use. A zero flash count means no lightning inside the area and window in `scope` -- report it as a quiet observation scoped to them, never as a data gap. Only call when storms may be active or the user asks about lightning. Example: {"location": "Tampa, FL"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

scope.description: Area and time window searched, so a zero count is unambiguous to report.

tools.name: get_map_snapshot
tools.title: Get map snapshot
tools.description: Render a weather map image for visual analysis. Simple form: pass `product` (a viz-catalog product_id like "mrms_qpe_01h_pass2_conus", "goes_truecolor_conus", "spc_day1_categorical", "hrrr_precip_hybrid_derived_conus" (future radar), "hrrr_subhourly_conus" (15-min Future Radar), "mrms_radar_nowcast_conus", "rtma_conus", "nbm_daily_temps", or "nexrad_l3:{SITE}:{PRODUCT}" for single-site radar, e.g. "nexrad_l3:TLX:N0B") plus a location and zoom (5=regional, 8=metro, 10=city). Composed form: pass `scene` -- a declarative scene document layering basemap + multiple weather products + active alerts + storm features + inline GeoJSON in one image (layers draw bottom-to-top, under basemap labels). Example scene: {"scene":"1.0","view":{"center":{"lat":43.8,"lon":-91.2},"zoom":8},"layers":[{"type":"weather","product":"goes_truecolor_conus"},{"type":"weather","product":"nexrad_l3:ARX:N0B"},{"type":"alerts","filter":{"events":["Tornado Warning"]},"onError":"skip"}]}. Alert filters (all optional, AND-combined): `ids` (specific alerts), `events`, `severities`, `minSeverity` (Extreme>Severe>Moderate>Minor>Unknown). Single-site radar keys: the address is `nexrad_l3:{SITE}:{KEY}` where KEY is `N{tilt}{measurement}` and tilt 0 is the 0.5 degree sweep -- N0B reflectivity (dBZ, where and how heavy), N0G base velocity (knots toward/away from the radar), N0S storm-relative velocity (storm motion removed, so a couplet is rotation rather than translation -- prefer it for rotation questions), N0C correlation coefficient (0-1, debris and hail), N0X differential reflectivity (dB). Legacy codes (N0V, N0R, N0Q) are accepted as aliases. Not every site produces every key; when a render reports which keys a site has, retry with one of those. Optional `time` (unix seconds): closest frame. Forecast (HRRR/nowcast/NBM) honors future times; analysis (MRMS/NEXRAD/RTMA/GOES) clamps to latest past. Pass `time` for future-radar asks — do not claim that capability is missing. Product ids must be real viz-catalog entries -- shorthand like "radar" or "reflectivity" is not one. Omit `product` for the default hybrid precip still. For Alaska and Hawaii prefer a local site or `mrms_precip_hybrid_derived_alaska` over CONUS mosaics, which do not cover them. Returns the rendered image plus per-layer resolved valid times.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

time.description: Unix seconds; closest frame (default: latest). Forecasts honor future times.

scene.description: Full scene document (composed form). When set, product/location/zoom are ignored.

tools.name: get_observations
tools.title: Get station observations
tools.description: METAR surface observations from weather stations: temperature, wind, visibility, ceiling, flight category, raw METAR. Nearest mode (default) returns the closest N stations to a location; station mode returns history for a specific ICAO identifier. Examples: {"location": "Denver, CO", "n": 3} or {"station": "KJFK", "hours": 6}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

n.description: Number of nearest stations (1-10). Default 1. Ignored in station mode.

station.description: ICAO station identifier (e.g. KJFK). Switches to station-history mode.

hours.description: Hours of history in station mode (1-24).

tools.name: get_observed_precipitation
tools.title: Observed precipitation
tools.description: How much rain fell: observed precipitation totals at a location. Use for "did it rain", "how much rain fell", "rain in the last 24 hours / since yesterday". Source: MRMS MultiSensor QPE Pass2 (radar bias-corrected to rain gauges) over 1/3/6/24/48/72 h windows (CONUS; 1 h only in Alaska and Hawaii). Values have about 2 mm (0.08 in) resolution, so 0 means under about 1 mm; data runs about an hour behind real time. Pass `at` (within 33 h) for totals ending at a past time (newest frame up to 3 h before it). With include_nowcast (default) it also returns a next-hour radar nowcast (CONUS): peak intensity (light/moderate/heavy), type and start time, not an amount. Forecast totals past the next hour: get_period_totals (planning); station reports: get_observations (observed).

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

windows.description: Accumulation windows ending at the latest frame (or at `at`).

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

at.description: RFC3339 end time within the last 33 h. Default: latest.

tools.name: get_outlooks
tools.title: Get hazard outlooks
tools.description: Hazard outlooks affecting a location. severe: SPC convective (day 1-8 categorical + tornado/wind/hail probabilities); fire: SPC fire weather; rain: WPC Excessive Rainfall (days 1-3); heat: NWS HeatRisk index (0-4, days 1-7); temperature/precipitation: CPC 6-10 day, 8-14 day, week 3-4 and monthly outlooks (favored category + probability bin; period=seasonal: 3-month leads). include_narrative=true adds the forecaster discussion (SWO, FWD, QPFERD, or the period's CPC PMD). Empty means no outlook covers the point, not a failure. Examples: {"location": "Moore, OK", "hazard": "severe", "include_narrative": true} or {"location": "Denver, CO", "hazard": "temperature"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

hazard.description: Hazard family (see description). Default severe; with period, both CPC hazards.

day.description: Outlook day for the narrative filter (1-8). Default 1.

include_narrative.description: Include the forecaster narrative (all hazards but heat).

period.description: Temperature/precipitation only. Default: all but seasonal.

tools.name: get_path_exposure
tools.title: Get path exposure
tools.description: Civic POIs (schools, hospitals, airports, …) inside a caller-supplied GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon. Not enabled for every caller: when off it returns 403 flag-disabled. Clip first; it does not derive HeatRisk areas. Optional classes filters the civic allowlist. Example: {"geometry":{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-88.15,41.77],[-88.14,41.77],[-88.14,41.78],[-88.15,41.78],[-88.15,41.77]]]},"classes":["school"]}.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon. Clip national outlooks first.

classes.description: Optional civic classes: airport, station, hospital, school, university, library, museum, stadium, cemetery, place_of_worship, camp_site, golf, attraction.

tools.name: get_period_totals
tools.title: Get period totals
tools.description: Aggregate a weather variable over one or more time periods. Returns server-computed totals, maxima, minima, or averages per period. Period start/end times should use the user's local timezone boundaries (not UTC midnight). Response includes the converted value and unit per period. Period-ending totals (1 h rain/snow, MRMS QPE) add whole windows; off-grid periods error naming the grid. Rain/snow/ice sums use 6 h QPF buckets if the model has them (source_variable), as get_forecast daily totals do; a bucket an edge cuts adds its share (approximate: true). Past the data: partial: true, frames_used/frames_expected, covered_start/covered_end. Ideal for questions like "total rainfall today and tomorrow" or "peak wind speed this weekend". For rain that already fell, use get_observed_precipitation. Accepts a place name directly. Example: {"location": "Portland, OR", "variable": "precipitation", "aggregation": "sum", "periods": [{"start": "2026-07-08T07:00:00Z", "end": "2026-07-09T07:00:00Z", "label": "Today"}]}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

variable.description: Standard variable name (e.g. precipitation, snowfall, temperature_2m, wind_speed_10m, cape).

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. Default sum. Use sum for precipitation/snowfall, max for temperature/wind, min for low temperatures, avg for humidity/cloud cover.

units.description: Units of every value in and out: imperial (default; °F, mph, in) or metric (°C, km/h, mm). si is deprecated and will be removed; use metric.

dataset_id.description: Dataset override. Default: auto-resolved NBM for the location.

attribution.description: Attribution the dataset licence requires. Cite it when quoting these values.

tools.name: get_platform_status
tools.title: Get platform status
tools.description: Current data-freshness status of the weather platform: overall state, per-source states (ok / degraded / outage / no_signal), open incidents with cause attribution (provider outage vs internal processing delay), and active provider advisories. Use this when a user asks whether data is current, when other tools return surprisingly stale data, or before presenting time-critical weather. If a source is degraded or in outage, tell the user their data may be stale rather than presenting it as live. No inputs. Refreshed about every 5 minutes.

include_ok.description: true: list every monitored source including healthy ones. false (default): only sources that are not ok, keeping the response compact.

overall.description: Worst state across customer-facing data sources; "unknown" when status is unavailable.

generated_at.description: When the status document was generated (UTC).

warming.description: true when no_signal only means monitoring is still warming up (not an outage).

tools.name: get_population_exposure
tools.title: Get population exposure
tools.description: National population-exposure headline for a risk-zone outlook product: how many people are inside risk bands at or above min_level. Powers headlines like "~57M people under major heat risk tomorrow". hazard=heat covers NWS HeatRisk days 1-3 (levels: 1 minor, 2 moderate, 3 major, 4 extreme). Pass product_id directly for other risk-zone products. Example: {"hazard": "heat", "min_level": 3}.

hazard.description: Hazard family (expands the day-1..3 product set). Currently: heat (HeatRisk).

product_id.description: Explicit risk-zone product ID (overrides hazard), e.g. heatrisk_day1_conus.

min_level.description: Minimum risk level to count (>=). Default 1 (any elevated risk).

tools.name: get_sounding
tools.title: Get radiosonde sounding
tools.description: Nearest RAOB (radiosonde) vertical soundings to a point. Each sounding carries: profile (pressure-indexed thermodynamics: pressure, height, temperature, dewpoint, wind arrays), wind_profile (height-indexed winds for hodographs/shear), and derived indices (sbcape/mucape/mlcape + cin, lifted_index, k_index, total_totals, pwat, freezing_level, lcl/lfc/el, bulk_shear_0_6km). Key suffixes name units; pressure levels stay hPa. Soundings launch at 00Z/12Z so data can be hours old. Example: {"location": "Norman, OK"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

tools.name: get_sounding_chart
tools.title: Get sounding chart
tools.description: Render the nearest RAOB (radiosonde) sounding as a Skew-T log-P + hodograph chart image for visual analysis: temperature/dewpoint traces, wind barbs, height-banded hodograph, and a derived-indices table (CAPE/CIN, lifted index, PWAT, shear, LCL). Soundings launch at 00Z/12Z so data can be hours old. Use get_sounding for the raw profile numbers. Example: {"location": "Norman, OK"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

units.description: Axis and summary: imperial (default; °F) or metric (°C); keys end in their unit.

scale.description: Raster scale factor (2 = retina; higher = larger image payload)

tools.name: get_storm_cells
tools.title: Get storm cells
tools.description: Radar-identified storm cells near a location, merging NEXRAD Level III algorithm output from the nearest radar site: storm tracks (cell position, movement, forecast positions), hail index (probability of hail/severe hail + max expected size), mesocyclone detections (rotation), and TVS (tornado vortex signatures). Use during active convection to see what the radar algorithms flag. An empty result means no detected cells -- common outside active storms. Example: {"location": "Norman, OK"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

include.description: Which detection families to include. Default: all.

summary.description: Ready-to-use one-liner. States explicitly when nothing was detected.

tools.name: get_storm_reports
tools.title: Get storm reports
tools.description: Recent NWS Local Storm Reports (LSRs) -- verified reports of tornadoes, hail, damaging winds, flooding near a location. Use to confirm severe weather occurrence or assess reported damage. valid_time is event occurrence (UTC); cite in local time. Example: {"location": "Wichita, KS", "hours": 12, "type": "H"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

type.description: Report type filter: T=tornado, H=hail, W=wind, F=flood, D=damage, S=snow.

tools.name: get_time_context
tools.title: Get time context
tools.description: Complete temporal context for a location: local time, timezone, 14-day calendar with day names and Today/Tomorrow offsets, sunrise/sunset/solar times (from the weather pipeline's astro product), and moon phase. Use whenever you need to reason about dates, times, or daylight for a location -- including "what time is sunset?", "is it dark there now?", or "what day of the week is the 4th-day forecast?". If current_time.timezone_resolved is false, zone unknown: state times as UTC, never as local. Accepts a place name directly. Example: {"location": "Seattle, WA"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

tools.name: get_tropical
tools.title: Get tropical activity
tools.description: Active NHC and CPHC tropical systems: forecast cones, track lines, forecast points, coastal watches/warnings, and 7-day Tropical Weather Outlook formation areas -- Atlantic, East and Central Pacific. Each feature carries a kind (cone | track | points | watch_warning | outlook_area) plus storm name, intensity, and timing properties. include_geometry=true adds full GeoJSON geometries (large). An empty result means no active tropical activity. Aircraft reconnaissance fixes and flight-level observations are in `get_tropical_observations`. Example: {} or {"include_geometry": true}.

include_geometry.description: Include full GeoJSON geometries (cone/track polygons). Default false.

tools.name: get_tropical_observations
tools.title: Get tropical observations
tools.description: Hurricane Hunter aircraft reconnaissance for active Atlantic and East Pacific systems: vortex data message (VDM) center fixes — pressure, max flight-level wind, eye — and high-density (HDOB) flight-level observations. These are aircraft measurements, not surface weather stations (use `get_observations` for METAR). Use `get_tropical` for NHC/CPHC cones, tracks, and watches; this tool is what the aircraft measured. kind=hdob returns the newest 200 records (about 1–2 h of flight; `truncated` says when more exist). Empty when no aircraft has flown in the window.

storm.description: ATCF id (al14) or storm name (polo). Unnumbered USAF missions never match.

kind.description: vdm = vortex fixes; hdob = flight-level obs; all = both. Default vdm.

tools.name: list_datasets
tools.title: List datasets
tools.description: Discover the gridded datasets (model grids, analyses) available at a location, or every public one when none is given, keyed by dataset_id. At a point: its domain (CONUS/Alaska/Hawaii) plus global grids, with freshness where tracked (latest model run as latest_run, latest_time, data_age_seconds, freshness_status). Use this to find dataset_id values for query_dataset or check whether data is current. Variables, units and standard names come from describe_dataset. Example: {"location": "Anchorage, AK"}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

include_freshness.description: Include latest model run and data age where tracked. Default true.

data_status.description: Present only when freshness was asked for and the data service did not provide it, or answered from a cached copy.

tools.name: query_dataset
tools.title: Query dataset
tools.description: Raw time series of one dataset's variables at a point, with unit labels: any gridded product (NBM, HRRR, RRFS, GFS, RTMA, MRMS, air quality, ...). Time modes: hours (default 24), time_start+time_end (ISO 8601), or latest=true (newest value). Up to 168 frames: when truncated, send next_cursor as cursor with the same arguments. reference_time pins a model run; each series reports its run (reference_time, or reference_times when runs mix); runs older than about 48 h may be gone. For blended forecasts use get_forecast. Examples: {"location": "Denver, CO", "dataset_id": "rrfs_surface", "variables": ["temperature_2m"], "hours": 18} or {"lat": 41.4, "lon": -92.9, "dataset_id": "rtma_conus", "variables": ["temperature_2m"], "latest": true}.

location.description: Free-text place: "City, ST" (e.g. "Portland, OR"), US ZIP, venue/address where enabled, or "lat,lon". Use this OR lat+lon, not both.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

dataset_id.description: Default: the NBM dataset for the location (nbm_conus/nbm_alaska/nbm_hawaii). Discover with list_datasets.

variables.description: Standard names (e.g. temperature_2m, precipitation); see describe_dataset.

hours.description: Hours from now (1-264): ahead, or back on analyses (default: newest 166 frames); from the run start with reference_time.

latest.description: Only the newest value (analyses like RTMA/MRMS).

reference_time.description: Pin a specific model run (ISO 8601). Default: latest run.

unit_labels.description: Unit of each variable in data.

reference_time.description: Model run behind every value in this series.

reference_times.description: Distinct runs, when this series mixes more than one.

status.description: ok, unavailable, out_of_domain (see related) or not_public.

related.description: With out_of_domain: a dataset that covers the point.

data_status.description: Present only when the data service did not answer and a cached copy was served.

attribution.description: Attribution the dataset licence requires. Cite it when quoting these values.

tools.name: reverse_geocode
tools.title: Reverse geocode
tools.description: Resolve coordinates to a human-readable place (city, state, county, timezone). Use when you have lat/lon but need a display name or the local timezone. Example: {"lat": 39.74, "lon": -104.99} -> Denver, Colorado, America/Denver.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). Most tools also accept a `location` place-name string instead of lat/lon.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). For continental US use negative values (west of the prime meridian).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.title: Search catalog
tools.description: Find which dataset answers a weather question when no dedicated tool fits: ranks the data catalog (model grids, radar, satellite, outlooks, observations) by the question's words and returns the best datasets with variable, units, cadence, a one-line why and the exact `call` (tool and arguments) to run next. Pass lat/lon, or `domain`, to keep only datasets covering the place; without one, Alaska/Hawaii twins fold into the CONUS dataset. Calls are ready for "now"; for a past time set `time_start`/`time_end` (or `at` where the tool supports it). Free; no network call.

query.description: The question or keywords, in the user's words.

lat.description: Latitude of the place (with lon).

lon.description: Longitude of the place (with lat).

domain.description: Coverage filter when there is no point; not with lat/lon.
The coverage filter applied: the point's domain, or `domain`.

call.description: The exact call that answers from this dataset. Absent when that tool is not on this connection; see `connect`.

toolset.description: With no `call`: the toolset whose tool answers this dataset.

connect.description: With no `call`: the path that serves this connection's toolsets plus that one, e.g. /x/core,catalog,guidance.

tools.name: search_locations
tools.title: Search locations
tools.description: Resolve a place to ranked candidates with lat/lon: city ("Denver"), "city, ST", ZIP ("50219"), or partial input with fuzzy=true ("bost" -> Boston); venues and addresses where enabled. Rows carry `type` place|zip|address|poi; pass a row's lat/lon to weather tools. `matched_via: "autosuggest"` marks rows found after the exact match missed; `partial` means a section timed out. Weather tools take `location` directly, venues included -- use this to disambiguate ("which Springfield?") or present choices.

query.description: Place query: city, "city, state", ZIP, partial text, or venue/address where enabled.

fuzzy.description: Autosuggest mode for partial/misspelled input. Default false (exact search).

near_lat.description: Rank venues/addresses near this point; pair with near_lon.

matched_via.description: Set on exact-search rows found by the venue/address fallback.

partial.description: Sections that did not finish, e.g. {"poi": "timeout"}; the list may be incomplete.
